learning_outcomes.description: Identify determinants of health, including impacts of social exclusion and marginalisation in Australia.

Describe roles in health and health-related settings in Australia, and priorities to build a resilient, sustainable, distributed and skilled health workforce, including digital health capabilities, health workforce wellbeing and retention.
Explain the structure and organisation of the Australian health care system, including regulation, infrastructure, governance, and funding.

Describe and demonstrate effective collaboration and interprofessional communication in a health context, including emphasising person-centred practices and including people, family, carers and communities as equal participants.
Recognise the different dimensions of cultural safety in health care practice and services, to advance Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples health outcomes.

assessments.assessment_title: Pre-class quizzes: IRATs (Individual Readiness Assurance Tests)
assessments.due_date: Week 1 quiz is formative. Week 2 - Week 13 features a weekly pre-class quiz or reflective tasks based on the self-directed online learning content for that week. 27/07/2026 - 26/10/2026
assessments.task_description:
Pre-class preparation: Individual Readiness Assurance Tasks (IRAT) or 'pre-class quizzes'

  • The aim of this assessment task is to ensure that students come prepared with a foundational understanding of the course material before engaging in deeper application exercises with their team during tutorials.
  • Students will have approximately five (5) questions or tasks each week. The questions will be in a multiple-choice, single-best-answer format.
  • There will be a formative (practice) IRAT to orientate you to the quiz platform in Week 1. This does not count to the overall IRAT total.
  • There will be 12 summative IRATs in total, spanning weeks 2-13.
  • IRATs will be marked as 0% (not attempted), 1% (minimal effort or incomplete) or 2% (satisfactory level of effort).
  • Each IRAT is worth up to 2% each, to a maximum total of 20%. Your top 10 IRAT results will be counted towards your final grade.

assessments.task_description:
The Collaborative Assessment consists of three parts with a combined weighting of 30% towards your grade.

1) Patient journey map - the patient journey map is a team assessment task where you illustrate the healthcare journey of ONE of the three key individuals whose journey we follow across the HLTH1000 tutorials. You will explore their interactions with the healthcare system, the healthcare workers involved in their care or service journey, pain points and opportunities for reform. The full task sheet is available on Blackboard.

This assessment component contributes up to 15% of your grade, and all team members receive the same mark.


2) Peer assessment factor - Using the UQ Buddy Check software, students will provide a rating and commentary on their own contribution and that of their peers to the team patient journey map task.

This assessment component contributes to 7.5% of your grade, and each student receives a unique result based on peer evaluation.


3) Tutor check-in with reflection - you will have TWO (2) brief 1:1 chats with your tutor. The first check in will take place half-way through semester and the second check-in will take place towards the end of semester. These will take place during your allocated tutorial time, where your tutor will check in on your reflections about your engagement with the course, team collaboration and developing cultural safety learning journey - examples of the questions will be made available on Blackboard.

The check-in halfway through semester is formative, and the check in towards the end of semester will contribute up to 7.5% of your grade.


Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task. Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing their assessment tasks (excluding the exam). Students must clearly reference any use of AI or MT in each instance.

A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.
assessments.submission_guidelines: The patient journey map only needs to be submitted by one team member. Submit online via Blackboard Assignments. All students in the team must contribute as agreed in the Team Contract.

Complete the weekly online self-directed learning prior to class. (TBL = weekly team-based learning tutorial)

Concepts of cultural awareness and cultural safety are fundamental to the provision of culturally appropriate health care.

learning_activities.topic:
Week 10 - Healthcare teams

There is no tutorial in week 10, but there is online learning to complete and a pre-class quiz. This quiz should be completed before the week 11 class.

Week 10 online learning focuses on teams in healthcare, and the different types and composition of teams. This includes uniprofessional, intraprofessional, multidisciplinary, interprofessional and transprofessional teams. We also look at the way these teams' function, and why it's important.


Learning outcomes: L02, L04

learning_activities.topic:
Week 11 - Collaborative healthcare settings

Complete the weekly online self-directed learning prior to class. (TBL = weekly team-based learning tutorial)

Week 11 explores real-world examples of collaboration in healthcare settings. These settings include aged care, rehabilitation and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Community Controlled Health Organisations, where collaboration occurs in closer proximity. We'll also look at settings which are highly collaborative, yet practitioners and/or care recipients may not be co-located. We'll analyse what the factors are that makes these teams successful.

Learning outcomes: L02, L04, L05
